Heard and perused the entire files.

2. By way of these two applications under Section 438 CrPC, the accused-applicants seek bail,
apprehending their arrest pursuant to FIR No.035 of 2021, under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC lodged at Police Station Kasana, District Gautam Budh Nagar.

sentences.text:
3. The FIR came to be registered pursuant to an order passed an an application under Section 156(3)
CrPC filed by the complainant.

Allegations in the FIR are that the father of the complainant had purchased a plot 420.14 mtr. in the year 2008 situated at Village Luksar, Tehsil Sadar, Police Station Greater Noida; after death of father of the complainant in the year 2012, the complainant became owner and got the possession of the said plot; the accused-applicants had good relation with the complainant; they used to visit the house of the complainant; the accused-applicants by playing fraud got the sale-deed registered of the said plot on 29.10.2020.
It was alleged that the accused-applicants had taken Rs. 15 Lakh, out of which they returned Rs.10 Lakh by cheque to the complainant.
4. The question in the present case is involved of registered sale-deed for consideration.

The prosecution story, as set up, does not appear to very convincing and, therefore, this Court finds that it is a fit case where the accused-applicants are to be enlarged on anticipatory bail inasmuch as charge-sheet has already been filed.

5. ALLOWED.
6.

The accused-applicants are directed to appear before the trial Court concerned within one week from today and if they do so, they shall be released on bail on each of them furnishing a personal bail bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, if not already filed, on the following conditions, which are imposed in the interest of justice, and other conditions,
which may be desirable by the learned trial Court:-
(i) the applicant(s) shall file an undertaking to the effect that they shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law;

(ii). the applicant(s) shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through their counsel.
In case of their absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against them under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;
(iii).

in case, the applicant(s) misuse(s) the liberty of bail and in order to secure their presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant(s) fail(s)
to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against them in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code; and (iv) the applicant(s) shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of their bail and proceed against them in Arun Singh vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134864443/
2 accordance with law.
